name: pi-agent-canvas
description: A dedicated cockpit for the pi coding agent: conversations as editor tiles, files it touches opening in the editor, and a session list in the activity bar.

Tip: focus this list and press Ctrl+F to filter.

piCanvas.disableBuiltInAi.markdownDescription: Disable VS Code's built-in AI/chat and the Copilot extensions (`chat.disableAIFeatures`), because this canvas replaces them. **Off by default** — this is the only VS Code setting the extension ever writes, and only when you turn this on. Turning it back off restores the setting if the extension was the one that changed it.

piCanvas.agentCommand.markdownDescription:
**The command used to start the agent server.** Empty means the built-in one (`node <extension>/scripts/pi-server.mjs`). Set it when the agent needs a particular environment — a login shell, a specific Node.js, or a wrapper that exports credentials.

It runs through your shell from `piCanvas.agentCwd`. Already in its environment: `PI_CANVAS_PORT`, `PI_CANVAS_CWD`, `PI_CANVAS_SERVER` (absolute path to the bundled server) and `PI_CANVAS_EXTENSION`, so a wrapper can `exec node "$PI_CANVAS_SERVER"`.

Not to be confused with `piCanvas.agentCwd`, which is a directory.

Example: `"bash -lc 'exec node \"$PI_CANVAS_SERVER\"'"`

piCanvas.agentCwd.markdownDescription:
**The directory the agent works in.** Empty means the first workspace folder. pi finds its project context (AGENTS.md), its extensions and its session store relative to this directory, so if the agent only behaves correctly in one repository, point this at it. `~` is expanded.

Not to be confused with `piCanvas.agentCommand`, which is the command used to start the server.

Example: `"/Users/me/work/agent-sandbox"`
